questions.q: How do you select multiple columns from a DataFrame at once?
options: Pass a list of column names in double square brackets, like df[["Product", "Revenue"]]
Use a comma inside single square brackets, like df["Product", "Revenue"]
Multiple columns can never be selected together, only one at a time
Use curly braces, like df{"Product", "Revenue"}
questions.explain: The outer brackets mean 'select columns,' and the inner brackets hold the actual list of column names — double brackets total.

options: Filters the DataFrame to only rows where Revenue is greater than 1500
Selects only the Revenue column
Deletes all rows where Revenue is greater than 1500
Creates a new column named 'Revenue > 1500'
questions.explain: Pandas evaluates the condition for every row and keeps only the rows where it evaluates to True — the same effect as a Power Query filter step.

questions.q: How do you combine two filter conditions in Pandas?
options: With & (and) or | (or), with parentheses around each individual condition
With Python's regular 'and' and 'or' keywords
Conditions can only be combined using a separate .combine() function
By writing them as two separate lines with no operator between them
questions.explain: Pandas requires & and |, not Python's and/or, because it evaluates the condition row by row rather than as a single boolean — and each condition needs its own parentheses.

questions.q: Why doesn't Python's regular 'and'/'or' work for combining Pandas filter conditions?
options: Because Pandas evaluates each condition across every row individually, not as one single True/False value the way 'and'/'or' expect
Because 'and'/'or' are reserved words that cause a syntax error in any context
Because DataFrames don't support boolean logic at all
It actually does work identically to & and |
questions.explain: Python's and/or expect a single boolean value, but a Pandas condition like df["Revenue"] > 1500 produces a whole column of True/False values — & and | are built to combine those element-by-element.

questions.q: What is the Power Query equivalent of df[df["Revenue"] > 1500]?
options: Clicking a column's filter arrow and setting a 'greater than 1500' condition
The Group By transform
The Merge Queries feature
There is no equivalent in Power Query
questions.explain: Both achieve the identical result — keeping only rows matching a condition — just through code instead of a clicked-through dialog.
